I can’t list “every peer-reviewed paper published in 2025 that cites *Attention Is All You Need*” from the evidence provided, because none of the gathered sources contain a complete, verifiable set of 2025 citing papers (nor full titles + full author lists for them). The evidence only points to unrelated pages and/or citation-count/context information, not the required 2025 peer-reviewed citing bibliography. [S1][S6][S10][S14]

What *is* supported by the evidence:
- The 2017 paper *Attention Is All You Need* exists (and is the one commonly cited), but the sources do not provide any 2025 citing-paper list. [S6][S10][S12]

What *cannot* be established from the evidence:
- Which specific 2025 publications cite the 2017 paper (i.e., a definitive list of citing works in 2025). [S19][S24]
- Which of those are peer-reviewed (vs. preprints/editorials/technical reports), and therefore cannot filter to “peer-reviewed papers only.” [S19][S25]
- For each peer-reviewed 2025 citing paper, the full title and full author list “as published.” (No such 2025 citing-paper metadata is present in the provided sources.) [S36][S38]

So, no accurate “every paper + full authors” answer can be produced without additional evidence (e.g., Crossref/ OpenAlex/ Semantic Scholar “cited by” results filtered to year=2025, with each record’s full bibliographic fields).
